facts.text: Kingston, Nevada sits at the mouth of Kingston Canyon, rising to about 5,961 feet, and is famed for its 19th‑century silver and gold mining.
In spring 1863, silver and gold were discovered in Kingston Canyon, prompting July claims at mines such as Victorine, Bi‑Metallic, and Goldpoint.
Kingston’s post office returned to its original name in 1863 and remained open until April 15, 1886.
During the 1930s, the CCC constructed a road from Kingston to Big Creek and set up a guard station 2.5 miles up the canyon.
Kingston lies in southern Lander County, on the northeast flank of the Toiyabe Range, just a few miles from the county’s highest peak, Bunker Hill.
Nevada State Route 376 skirts Kingston, heading north 20 mi to Austin and south 90 mi toward Tonopah.
